validity.array_size_assumed: 128 neuromorphic cores, 1024 neurons and 4096 in/out axons per core, 16 MB synaptic memory
validity.notes: Davies 2018 Table 2 is titled 'Loihi PRE-SILICON performance and energy measurements' and the text calls it SDF+SPICE simulation 'consistent with early post-silicon characterization'. Every per-event constant here is therefore a design-intent number, not a silicon measurement — which is exactly why measurement_kind is 'simulation' and a cross-platform comparison against TrueNorth (silicon) must disclose the difference. The static-power constant is the exception: it is derived from measured board-level data (Frady 2020).

e_neuron_update.note: 'Energy per neuron update (active / inactive) | 81 pJ / 52 pJ' -- ONE quantity at two activity levels, so it is one banded constant. Nominal takes the INACTIVE cost because the multiplicand is every neuron update, and a census cannot say which of them fired; charging all of them the active cost would over-charge every neuron that stayed silent, which in a sparse SNN is nearly all of them. The active figure is the band's upper corner, i.e. the all-firing worst case. e_leak_per_neuron_step is deliberately NOT declared: on Loihi it is this same measurement, and declaring both makes the pricer charge every neuron twice.

e_core_init.derivation: frady2020neuromorphic Table 2 reports the RESET phase energy of one query as a line of its own: 3.06 mJ on the 768-chip 1M-pattern configuration and 0.19 mJ on the 76,800-pattern one (76,800 = 48 x 1600, i.e. 48 chips). The paper states reset energy per chip is constant per query, and the two rows agree on that constant within 0.66% (3.984 vs 3.958 uJ per chip) -- an independent check that the decomposition is the paper's own. Per core at 128 neuromorphic cores per chip: 3.06e-3 / 768 / 128 = 31.13 nJ and 0.19e-3 / 48 / 128 = 30.92 nJ, which is the band. UPPER BOUND on the core's own share: the measured reset phase covers the whole system's preparation for the next query, including the embedded x86 work, and no published figure isolates the core-state clear inside it. Supersedes the looser compartment-sweep bound (1024 x 52 pJ = 53.2 nJ from Table 2's inactive neuron update), which this measurement shows to be ~1.7x high.
e_core_init.note: Energy to reset one core's neuron state at the start of a pass.

t_core_init.derivation: frady2020neuromorphic Sec 5.4: 'the reset time of 230us on Pohoiki Springs that falls off the latency critical path'. The framework charges core init per core (t_core_init x segment_cores), so the wall consistent with that model is the chip's share serialized over its 128 cores: 230 / 128 = 1.797 us. UPPER BOUND, twice over -- the published wall covers the whole reset phase (embedded x86 orchestration included), and the intra-chip parallelism is unstated, so a chip that clears its cores concurrently pays far less per core. The low corner is that bulk/parallel clear. This also refutes the compartment-sweep reading (1024 x 5.3 ns = 5.43 us per core), which would put a chip's serial reset at 695 us, three times the measured system wall.
t_core_init.note: Wall time to reset one core's neuron state at the start of a pass.

e_inter_tile_hop.note: 'Energy per tile hop (E-W / N-S) | 3.0 pJ / 4.0 pJ'. The mesh is anisotropic and a hop count does not say which axis it took, so the two published values ARE the band and the nominal is their mean. Collapsing them to one number would hide a 1.33x directional spread the paper measured.

t_hop.note: 'Latency per tile hop (E-W / N-S) | 4.1 ns / 6.5 ns' — the same anisotropy as the hop energy.

t_array_read.note: 'Time per synaptic spike op (max) | 3.5 ns'. Published as a MAXIMUM with no minimum; the band is a point at the published value rather than an invented spread downward.

t_sync_barrier.note: 'Mesh-wide barrier sync time (1-32 tiles) | 113-465 ns'. The band IS the published tile-count range; nominal takes the 32-tile end, since a real deployment spans the mesh rather than one tile.

host_compute_rate.derivation: identity: a measured host wall is used at face value (wall / 1.0)
host_compute_rate.note: The derate a MEASURED host wall is divided by. Identity by definition here: Loihi-hosted deployments measure their CPU walls end-to-end (frady2020neuromorphic Sec 5.4 states 220us + 300us on the latency critical path), and derating a measurement would invent headroom. Only the measured-wall pricing path reads this; no host THROUGHPUT rate (host_macs_per_s) is declared, so a run that never measured its wall still refuses host-inclusive axes by name.

t_cycle.note: 'the system typically sustains just over 13us per timestep for the 1M-pattern dataset workload and 5.8us per timestep when processing 76,800-pattern datasets.' MEASURED on Pohoiki Springs (768 chips, unthrottled). An asynchronous mesh has no device timestep constant, so this is a workload-dependent SUSTAINED per-timestep wall, not a clock: the band's ends are the two published workloads and nominal takes the LARGER (1M-pattern) figure, because the paper reports late-window slowdowns to ~60us (x86 spike-I/O bound, Fig 8) that a flat wall already under-charges. Single-chip barrier time is a different scale (113-465 ns, t_sync_barrier); throttled real-time mode is 1 ms/step (davies2021advancing Sec II-A). Owner decision 2026-08-16: declare the measured band rather than refuse latency outright; the paired knn latency reference case is SELF-CONSISTENCY (same paper).

membrane_bits.note: Membrane potential and current state are signed 24-bit registers (+/-2^23). Sourced from an independent non-Intel characterization rather than the architecture paper, which does not state the width.

conductance_levels.derivation: Loihi supports synaptic weights of up to 9 bits including sign, so a synapse takes 2^9 = 512 distinct values. Digital SRAM synapses, so this is a precision fact, not an analog conductance count.

write_sigma.derivation: Synapses live in digital SRAM ('The core's total SRAM capacity is 2 Mb, including ECC overhead'), so a written weight has no analog programming spread. Zero is a fact about the technology.

read_sigma.derivation: Digital SRAM read; no analog column-current sensing, so no read spread.

area_per_adc.derivation: 'All logic in the chip is digital' — there is no analog-to-digital converter in the datapath, so the count is zero by construction rather than unknown.

e_adc_conversion.derivation: No ADC exists in a Loihi core; see area_per_adc.

t_adc_conversion.derivation: No ADC exists in a Loihi core; see area_per_adc.

area_per_core_total.derivation: 60 mm^2 die / 128 neuromorphic cores = 0.46875 mm^2 = 468750 um^2 per core. This is a DIE-AREA SHARE, not a measured core layout: the die also carries three x86 cores and I/O, so the real neuromorphic core is smaller. Cross-checked against the paper's own 'maximum neuron density of 2,184 per mm^2': 1024 neurons / 0.46875 mm^2 = 2184.5 neurons/mm^2, reproducing it to four figures — which is what confirms the division is the one the authors made.
area_per_core_total.note: An upper bound on the per-core footprint. Supersedes the decomposed area constants.

area_global_fixed.derivation: The whole 60 mm^2 die is already attributed across the 128 cores by area_per_core_total (a die-area SHARE, not a core layout), so charging any of it again chip-wide would double-count the same measurement.

p_static_per_core.derivation: Measured board static power 3.34 W over 32 Loihi chips = 104.4 mW per chip; 104.4 mW / 128 cores = 815 uW per core. The paper attributes leakage to the cores: 'Almost all leakage can be attributed to the neuromorphic cores, which dominate chip area.'
p_static_per_core.note: An UPPER bound per core, and the only measured (not simulated) energy constant in this profile — the supply voltage of the board measurement is not stated.

p_static_global.derivation: The whole measured static power is already attributed per core, following the paper's own attribution; charging it again chip-wide would double-count one measurement.

e_mac.note: 'Energy per synaptic spike op (min) | 23.6 pJ'. This is a PER-OPERATION energy, not a whole-chip average: it does not contain the neuron-update or static power the same table reports separately, so it belongs beside them rather than superseding them. Published as a MINIMUM with no maximum, so the band is a point at the published value -- inventing an upper corner would fabricate the number the paper withheld, and a prediction built on a minimum is expected to land high.
